title: Understanding Linear Separability
text: Linear separability means that you can draw a straight line (or hyperplane in higher dimensions) to separate the classes in your dataset. Consider how transformations can help achieve this.

title: Effect of Transformation
text: Think about how the transformation $$(x_1,x_2)$$ to $$({x_2}^2,{x_1}^2)$$ affects the data points. Does it make it easier to separate the classes with a straight line?

title: Analyzing the Transformation
text: Consider a simple dataset where points are not linearly separable. Apply the transformation $$(x_1,x_2)$$ to $$({x_2}^2,{x_1}^2)$$. What happens to the points?

hintAnswer: The transformed points form a parabolic shape making them easier to separate with a line.
title: Visualizing the Transformation
text: Imagine plotting the original points and then plotting the transformed points. How does the shape of the data change?

title: Conclusion on Linear Separability
